title: Dark Chocolate, Raspberry and Champagne Cookies
story: Same flavor profile as the cake, less structural commitment. The champagne adds acidity without tasting like champagne, which is a more useful trick than it sounds. The dried raspberries hold their shape through the bake. Dust with powdered sugar right before serving — do it too early and you're just dusting twice.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
¼ cup champagne or dry sparkling wine

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, ½ cup cocoa powder, ½ tsp baking powder, and ¼ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter, ½ cup granulated sugar, and ½ cup packed brown sugar together until light and creamy, about 2–3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look pale and fluffy, not dense or grainy.

steps.text: Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each before adding the next.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract and ¼ cup champagne.
Fold in ½ cup dark chocolate chips and ¼ cup dried raspberries.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheet.

steps.donenessCue: The dark cocoa dough makes the edges hard to read by color — press the edge of one cookie gently with a finger. It should feel just firm while the center still has a little give. They firm up significantly as they cool.

steps.text: Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Dust with powdered sugar just before serving — don't dust too early or it absorbs into the surface.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Chill the dough for 30 minutes before rolling — it firms up the dough and the cookies spread less.
Use fresh raspberries instead of dried — fold them in gently at the very end. The cookies will be more delicate and the fruit more pronounced.
Roll the dough balls in cocoa powder before baking for a truffle-style finish — skip the powdered sugar dusting if you do.
Add the zest of 1 orange to the butter mixture — it bridges the chocolate and raspberry the same way it does in the cake version.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Dust with a fresh layer of powdered sugar before serving if they've been sitting. Freeze for up to 3 months; thaw at room temperature and re-dust before serving.
